## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mettasutta* ("The Benefits of Love", Iti 22; PTS It 14) is a discourse preserved in the *Ekakanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka*. In this teaching, the Buddha declares that "acts of merit" (*puñña*) is a synonym for everything that is blissful, desirable, pleasing, endearing, and charming. To illustrate the power of merit, the Buddha recounts the immense cosmic and heavenly fruits he personally experienced over many eons as a result of developing a mind of loving-kindness and performing meritorious deeds.

 The text is also cited in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37, *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*).

All twenty-two passages retrieved from the secondary literature corpus under the title *Mettasutta* concern the famous *Karaṇīyamettasutta* (Sn 1.8 / Khp 9) and its liturgical recitation as a *paritta*, rather than this discourse from the *Itivuttaka*.
